Bug_Title: EC: Call to equals() comparing different types (EC_UNRELATED_TYPES)
Bug_Details:
This method calls equals(Object) on two references of different
class types and analysis suggests they will be to objects of different classes
at runtime. Further, examination of the equals methods that would be invoked suggest that either
this call will always return false, or else the equals method is not symmetric (which is
a property required by the contract
for equals in class Object).
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by calling the equals() method on a String object with an Integer object as the argument. Since String and Integer are different types, this comparison will always return false and violates the symmetry property of the equals method.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the EqualsBugExample class. Inside the showBug method, the equals() method is called on a String object with an Integer object as the argument, which always returns false and violates the symmetry property of the equals method.
